STEP 1 - Scene: A small portion of cooked spinach (sautéed or wilted, with some bits of garlic/onion and a few pieces of red pepper and a broccoli floret) on a white square plate, photographed from above at a near-overhead angle. Only this plate is part of the meal; the partial plate at the left edge is not.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is about 26 cm across. Its usable width is roughly 26 cm, so the vessel area is about 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2. Treating the plate as roughly square, the area is similar (about 26 x 26 ≈ 676 cm^2 at the rim), so I use ~530 cm^2 as a conservative figure.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Spinach leaves (cooked/wilted, with a little oil)
- Garlic/onion bits (small)
- Red pepper pieces (a few)
- Broccoli floret piece (small)

STEP 4 - Area: The food pile covers roughly 30% of the plate: spinach ~26%, red pepper ~1%, broccoli ~2%, garlic/onion ~1%. Total ≈ 30% ≈ 160 cm^2.

STEP 5 - Volume: The spinach pile is fairly tall and loose, about 3 cm high on average.
- Spinach: 0.26 x 530 = 138 cm^2 x 3 cm ≈ 414 ml
- Red pepper: ~5 cm^2 x 0.5 cm ≈ 3 ml
- Broccoli: ~11 cm^2 x 1.5 cm ≈ 16 ml
- Garlic/onion: ~5 cm^2 x 0.3 cm ≈ 2 ml

STEP 6 - Grams (bulk densities):
- Spinach (cooked, loose leafy greens): 414 ml x 0.15 ≈ 62 g
- Red pepper: 3 ml x 0.6 ≈ 2 g
- Broccoli: 16 ml x 0.6 ≈ 10 g
- Garlic/onion: 2 ml x 0.6 ≈ 1 g

Total ≈ 75 g.

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Spinach, cooked, ~23 kcal/100 g: 62 g → ~14 kcal
- Red pepper, ~31 kcal/100 g: 2 g → ~1 kcal
- Broccoli, ~35 kcal/100 g: 10 g → ~3.5 kcal
- Garlic/onion, ~40 kcal/100 g: 1 g → ~0.4 kcal
- Oil residue: a little visible sheen, maybe 2 g x 880 kcal/100 g ≈ 18 kcal

Total ≈ 37 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A modest, partly eaten side of cooked greens on a large plate, with about 75 g total and about 35–40 kcal, is plausible. Leafy greens are low in energy, and the oil adds most of the calories.
